title: MZ Requesting official clarification on using RTP from different RPG Maker versions in a commercial game

posts.author: Miky_Joe
posts.body:
Hello,
I legally own multiple RPG Maker versions (including VX Ace and MZ).
I would like to receive an
official confirmation
regarding the following point:
If I legally own both versions, am I allowed to use default RTP (materials/assets) from RPG Maker VX Ace inside a commercial game created with RPG Maker MZ?
I am aware that the RPG Maker FAQ states:
“As long as you own the version of RPG Maker you are using, and the version of RPG Maker you are using materials from, you are free to use any default materials that came with those purchases within the RPG Maker series.”
Click to expand...
However, the wording in the MZ EULA (“Company Assets contained in this Software may be used only in User Games produced with This Software”) appears more restrictive.
Therefore, I would like to request an
official, written clarification
confirming whether:
I can legally use VX Ace RTP inside an RPG Maker MZ game,
and whether I can sell a commercial game made this way,
without violating any license terms or facing legal consequences.
A clear statement from your team will help me proceed correctly and ensure compliance with RPG Maker’s licensing terms.
Thank you very much.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body: Baz has a video on YouTube going over the latest EULA saying you can use RPG Maker assets in ANY engine (e.g. Unity, Godot, etc) as long as you own the engine they came from. Baz is a mod on the official RPG Maker Guild forums (GGG's forums).

posts.author: Miky_Joe
posts.body:
I don't know who "Baz" is, nor do I know if he works in Kadokawa's legal department. I'd heard it was possible, but I can't find an official response. A YouTube video doesn't protect you from legal issues; that's what I mean. Is there an official statement, or an explicit section that clearly and directly addresses this?
Anyway, thank you very much for responding, but it seems no one is interested in this topic, since many users have this same question.

posts.author: AquaEcho
posts.body: The YouTube video shows where exactly it says in the fine print that you can use them in any engine. You can read it yourself. Otherwise email Kadokawa or GGG and hope their legal department responds. I doubt their lawyers are chilling out on these forums.

The video does NOT point out exactly. However, when you go to the GGG site/license you can find it relatively easily.
Article 5 (License)​
We hereby license the User who has purchased the GGG Products in an authorized manner as recognized by us to use the GGG Products as follows:
A. To create an original game (the “User Game”) using the GGG Products (including the computer programs that make up the GGG Products) and the materials contained in the GGG Products (text, music, images, etc. collectively, “Our Material”). When using Our Material, the User shall comply with these Material Terms in the attached Supplementary Provisions of these Terms.
B. To reproduce, transfer, sell, rent out, publicly present, transmit to the public, or make the User Game created under the preceding item available for transmission (collectively, “Distribution, etc.”) whether paid for or for free. However, in this case, the User shall comply with the Game Distribution Terms in the attached Supplementary Provisions of these Terms.
DrFreeman said:

Click to expand...
So even in the video it calls out there's a difference between where you got the game from. The RPGMakerWeb stuff is old Degica/Komodo; so if you bought the standalone RM from their website, you're probably beholden to it. If you bought it from GGG or Steam, then you're using the the one from RPGMakerOfficial. Even if you bought it on steam before the change, GGG is listed on the steam store now so GGG license covers that now.
TL;DR - If you bought RM from Degica Shop (or Komodo) you're on the old EULA and MZ RTP can only be used on RMMZ; but other RTPs would fall under their own EULA, so if they say you can use assets on other RMs, then you can use them on MZ.
If you bought RM on GGG or Steam, it's all transferable (read Article 5 above).

That's not how EULAs work. Software doesn't have different licensing depending on which store you bought it from.
There is one EULA which is the most current one written by the company that
makes the software
. Whether that is correctly updated by other distribution platforms is irrelevant. Both versions of the EULA say that Gotcha Gotcha Games made the software, and site for Gotcha Gotcha Games says their EULA applies to their products. There's no reason for question there.
KawasakiNinja said:
(read Article 5 above).
Click to expand...
That quote is not germane to the conversation - it's talking about the distribution
of your game
. I don't know how you read it to have anything to do with RTP material.
The question in this thread is about use of RTP assets which is addressed in
the current terms and conditions
under Material Terms and Conditions:
Buying the software from the Komodo Plaza (or previously from Degica) is absolutely an authorized manner, those publishers are an authorized distributor of the software. That's why they haven't been sued off the Internet. There is nothing in the text of the EULA that says you must buy it in some specific way or from a specific place, only that you have bought it legally.
